capabilities.title: Bootstrap, location, tags, and deployment metadata
capabilities.description: Required deployment identity, locations, tags, deployment topology, release, and stable resource token contracts. Defaults and allowed values are the values on the cited pinned Bicep parameters.
identityRbacAssertions: principalId and principalType are cataloged separately under identity-rbac.
networkAssertions: deploymentMode=standalone does not itself enable isolation; networkIsolation controls the two assessed topologies.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Terraform cannot instantiate the public standalone topology.

defaultDifferences: Bicep deploymentMode defaults standalone; Terraform flag_platform_landing_zone defaults true and false selects its network-isolated standalone approximation.

scenarioAssessments.blockedReason: Terraform v0.5.1 structurally requires a VNet, subnets, private endpoints, and mostly disabled public network access, so it cannot represent Bicep standalone-standard.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Terraform accepts location, resource-group, tags, naming prefix, and a topology flag, but exposes only five sparse outputs; resource_id is the literal string tbd.

defaultDifferences: Terraform resource_id output is the literal string tbd.

capabilities.title: CAF and legacy resource naming
capabilities.description: CAF/legacy mode, deterministic tokens, explicit resource names, and the names surfaced to consumers. Exact defaults and resource-specific limits remain pinned in main.bicep/main.json.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Naming alone does not remove Terraform's mandatory private topology.

defaultDifferences: Bicep supports caf and legacy modes with explicit per-resource overrides; Terraform exposes one nullable name_prefix.

scenarioAssessments.blockedReason: Terraform's naming contract is only usable inside its mandatory VNet/private-endpoint topology, which cannot produce standalone-standard.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Terraform name_prefix cannot preserve Bicep CAF/legacy mode and all explicit resource-name overrides.

capabilities.title: Standard versus network-isolated standalone topology
capabilities.description: The networkIsolation=false public baseline and networkIsolation=true VNet/private endpoint/firewall/Bastion/NAT/private DNS baseline are distinct and assessed independently.
networkAssertions: standalone-standard has public access and no mandatory VNet, private endpoints, firewall, Bastion, NAT, or private DNS.
standalone-network-isolated has a VNet, private endpoints, firewall, Bastion, NAT, and private DNS.
Terraform flag_platform_landing_zone=false approximates only standalone-network-isolated.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Consumers cannot request the Bicep public, no-VNet standalone shape.

defaultDifferences: Bicep networkIsolation defaults false; Terraform service public network defaults are mostly false while private endpoints are always created.

scenarioAssessments.blockedReason: Terraform v0.5.1 always creates Foundry private endpoints and requires VNet/subnet inputs; its service defaults disable public access, so networkIsolation=false has no analogue.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: The broad private shape exists, but Terraform has no networkIsolation contract and service-level access controls differ.

capabilities.title: VNet, subnet names, prefixes, delegation, and existing VNet
capabilities.description: All VNet/subnet name and address surfaces, existing-VNet reuse, and subnet deployment controls.
networkAssertions: Container Apps Environment delegation and private endpoint network policies are part of the subnet contract.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Terraform requires VNet and subnet structure even though Bicep standard requires none.
scenarioAssessments.blockedReason: Required Terraform vnet_definition and always-created private endpoints prevent a no-VNet standalone-standard deployment.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Terraform supports created/BYO VNet and subnet maps, but names, defaults, delegation, and side-by-side semantics differ.

capabilities.title: NSGs, routes, firewall, and egress rules
capabilities.description: NSG deployment, Azure Firewall/UDR egress, media egress, bootstrap/build FQDN extensions, and existing or external next-hop routes.
networkAssertions: Network-isolated standalone routes workload subnets through local or supplied egress and controls allowed destinations explicitly.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Terraform introduces routes and private network controls absent from standard.
scenarioAssessments.blockedReason: Terraform's required private network means its routing and firewall choices cannot yield Bicep's no-mandatory-network standalone-standard topology.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Terraform has NSG/firewall/route definitions but lacks Bicep's jumpbox/build/media egress presets and existing-route-table contract.

capabilities.title: Hub/spoke peering and gateway transit
capabilities.description: Optional spoke-to-hub peering, route ownership, gateway transit, and remote gateway controls.
identityRbacAssertions: Cross-subscription hub peering requires operator permissions outside the spoke deployment.
networkAssertions: The reverse hub-to-spoke peering remains operator/platform-owned in the Bicep contract.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: This optional integration does not create a standard topology in Terraform.
scenarioAssessments.blockedReason: Terraform still requires its spoke VNet and private endpoints; peering options cannot remove them for standalone-standard.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Terraform supports VNet/vWAN peering but uses a different aggregate contract and ownership model.

capabilities.title: Private DNS creation, BYO zones, policy ownership, and links
capabilities.description: Policy-managed DNS, fifteen granular BYO private-zone IDs, link suffixing, zone groups, and link ownership.
networkAssertions: Bicep can create, reuse, or defer DNS zone groups to policy; shared-zone links are explicitly consumer-owned when BYO IDs are used.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Terraform mandates private endpoint DNS behavior where standard needs no private DNS.

defaultDifferences: Bicep creates private DNS only when isolated and defaults to module ownership; Terraform creates or references private zones as part of its mandatory private topology.

scenarioAssessments.blockedReason: Mandatory Terraform private endpoints require private DNS decisions, unlike Bicep standalone-standard's public topology.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Terraform supports created/existing/policy-linked zones, but namespace coverage, defaults, link naming, and ownership differ.

defaultDifferences: Terraform private_endpoints_manage_dns_zone_group defaults true; Bicep policyManagedPrivateDns defaults false and applies across local zone/group creation.

capabilities.title: Private endpoint location, resource group, ordering, and service coverage
capabilities.description: Private endpoint placement, subnet use, DNS zone groups, and serialized dependencies for all supported services.
networkAssertions: Bicep creates private endpoints only when networkIsolation is true and preserves service dependency ordering.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Terraform private endpoints cannot be disabled to obtain the public standard baseline.
scenarioAssessments.blockedReason: Foundry create_private_endpoints=true and required private endpoint subnet structure make private endpoints structural in Terraform v0.5.1.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Terraform creates private endpoints but does not expose equivalent cross-region/resource-group placement and ordering controls.

capabilities.title: Jumpbox, Bastion, and NAT Gateway
capabilities.description: Independent nullable component flags, legacy deployVM fallback, BYO IDs, Bastion access/SKU/tunneling, and VM configuration.
identityRbacAssertions: Jumpbox receives explicit managed identity and scoped operational roles when deployed.
networkAssertions: Bicep isolated defaults derive Bastion and NAT from jumpbox selection; standard deploys none by default.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Even with Terraform jump resources disabled, mandatory VNet/private endpoints remain.
scenarioAssessments.blockedReason: Terraform cannot remove the underlying private topology to produce standalone-standard; jumpbox/Bastion flags do not change that constraint.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Terraform has jump VM and Bastion definitions but no equivalent independent NAT/BYO/legacy fallback contract.

capabilities.title: Optional Application Gateway WAF ingress
capabilities.description: Default-off aggregate public ingress, WAF, TLS, allow-list, identity, subnet, and automation outputs.
identityRbacAssertions: Gateway identity receives certificate-secret access only when live TLS ingress is configured.
networkAssertions: Empty source prefixes keep the default-off gateway skeleton inert; explicit sources and certificate activate HTTPS.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Terraform Application Gateway exists only with its required private landing-zone topology.
scenarioAssessments.blockedReason: Terraform's Application Gateway option cannot be combined with a no-VNet/no-private-endpoint standard deployment.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Terraform exposes Application Gateway/WAF definitions but not the same aggregate activation semantics and output set.

capabilities.title: Foundry account, project, and agent service
capabilities.description: Foundry account/project flags, project metadata, agent-service flag, account local-auth posture, and core project outputs.
identityRbacAssertions: Bicep defaults to Entra-only Foundry authentication and assigns project/account roles explicitly.
networkAssertions: Foundry public access follows networkIsolation and allowedIpRanges in Bicep.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Terraform Foundry always requests private endpoints and cannot match public standalone.

defaultDifferences: Bicep aiFoundryDisableLocalAuth defaults true; Terraform local_auth_enabled defaults true.
Bicep deployAAfAgentSvc defaults true; Terraform create_ai_agent_service defaults false.

scenarioAssessments.blockedReason: Terraform Foundry create_private_endpoints=true plus mandatory VNet/subnet inputs prevents the standalone-standard Foundry account topology.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Account and project are supported, but local-auth and agent-service defaults invert Bicep behavior.

defaultDifferences: Bicep aiFoundryDisableLocalAuth defaults true; Terraform local_auth_enabled defaults true.
Bicep deployAAfAgentSvc defaults true; Terraform create_ai_agent_service defaults false.

capabilities.title: Foundry models, connections, and BYOR dependencies
capabilities.description: Model deployments, Search/Bing/knowledge connections, and existing Search, Storage, and Cosmos dependency IDs including Foundry BYOR storage SKU.
identityRbacAssertions: Bicep adds cross-service Foundry, Search, Storage, and Cosmos role assignments needed by configured connections.
networkAssertions: BYOR resources remain responsible for compatible private connectivity when supplied.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Supported nested Foundry features remain enclosed by mandatory Terraform private topology.
scenarioAssessments.blockedReason: Terraform cannot deploy these Foundry nested resources without its structurally required VNet and private endpoints.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Terraform has nested model/connection/BYOR fields but no complete Bicep list contract or automatic cross-service RBAC equivalent.

defaultDifferences: Terraform Foundry BYOR storage defaults ZRS with shared access keys disabled; this is distinct from Terraform standalone GenAI storage.

capabilities.title: AI Search, Bing grounding, and Speech
capabilities.description: Feature flags, region overrides, Speech SKU allowed values, connections, endpoints, names, regions, and resource IDs.
identityRbacAssertions: Search and Speech identities and deploying principal receive explicit data-plane roles in Bicep.
networkAssertions: Speech and Search use disabled public access plus private endpoints when isolated.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Terraform cannot offer these services in Bicep's public no-VNet baseline.
scenarioAssessments.blockedReason: Terraform service topology depends on required VNet/private endpoints and mostly disabled public access, preventing standalone-standard.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Search and grounding constructs are sparse and no equivalent standalone Speech service/output contract was found.

capabilities.owner: AI Landing Zone data and AI maintainers

capabilities.title: Container Apps environment and workloads
capabilities.description: Container Apps Environment, workload profiles, external workload list, per-app ingress/Dapr/identity behavior, and workload outputs.
identityRbacAssertions: Each Bicep workload receives managed identity, registry pull, runtime configuration, and optional per-app Key Vault access.
networkAssertions: Bicep environment is external in standard and internal/VNet-integrated with a private endpoint in isolated mode.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Terraform supplies only an environment and cannot create the Bicep workloads; its global private topology also blocks standard.
scenarioAssessments.blockedReason: Terraform v0.5.1 requires the landing-zone VNet/private endpoints and has no Container Apps workload resources, so it cannot represent Bicep standalone-standard workloads.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Terraform deploys only the Container Apps Environment, not container apps, ingress, Dapr, workload identities, or workload outputs.

capabilities.title: Runtime configuration modes and App Configuration population
capabilities.description: appConfig/containerEnv/none allowed values, App Configuration store, labels, passthrough values, direct bootstrap env vars, and generated runtime keys.
identityRbacAssertions: appConfig mode grants each workload App Configuration Data Reader; deployment principal receives Data Owner.
networkAssertions: Deploy-time App Configuration population occurs only outside isolation; isolated consumers populate through post-provision paths.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Terraform creates an App Configuration store but neither Bicep's runtime modes nor populated settings/workloads.
scenarioAssessments.blockedReason: Terraform's required private topology prevents the standard scenario, and no App Configuration key-value population/runtime-mode implementation exists.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: No App Configuration key-value population or appConfig/containerEnv/none runtime configuration mode exists in Terraform.

capabilities.title: Foundry IQ and retrieval-backend configuration
capabilities.description: Retrieval backend, Foundry IQ pattern/API/billing/source/storage/search/filter/security configuration, generated keys, connections, and outputs.
identityRbacAssertions: Bicep connects Foundry project, Search, and storage identities for configured knowledge sources.
networkAssertions: Knowledge endpoints follow the selected Search/Foundry private connectivity.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: No Terraform runtime configuration exists and the standard topology is structurally unavailable.
scenarioAssessments.blockedReason: Terraform requires private topology and has no Foundry IQ/retrieval-backend runtime configuration contract, so standalone-standard cannot be represented.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: No Foundry IQ or retrieval-backend configuration, generated keys, or equivalent outputs were found.

capabilities.title: Cosmos DB, Storage, Key Vault, and containers
capabilities.description: Feature flags, existing Key Vault, Cosmos database/throughput/analytical storage, and Storage/Cosmos container lists.
identityRbacAssertions: Bicep centralizes control-plane and Cosmos data-plane assignments and avoids runtime account keys by default where supported.
networkAssertions: Public access and IP rules follow networkIsolation/allowedIpRanges; isolated services receive private endpoints.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Terraform service defaults disable public access and require private endpoints.

defaultDifferences: Terraform standalone GenAI storage defaults GRS with shared access keys enabled; Foundry BYOR storage defaults ZRS with shared access keys disabled.

scenarioAssessments.blockedReason: Terraform GenAI Storage, Cosmos, and Key Vault default to disabled public access and private endpoints in the mandatory VNet, preventing standalone-standard.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Core accounts exist, but database/container shaping, runtime keys, and automatic data-plane RBAC differ.

defaultDifferences: Terraform standalone GenAI storage defaults GRS with shared access keys enabled; Foundry BYOR storage defaults ZRS with shared access keys disabled.

capabilities.owner: AI Landing Zone data and AI maintainers

capabilities.title: Container Registry and private ACR Task builds
capabilities.description: Registry feature, ACR Task agent pool name/tier/count, private build subnet, and registry endpoint/resource outputs.
identityRbacAssertions: Workloads and hosted-agent identities receive registry pull; build operators receive scoped task permissions.
networkAssertions: Bicep uses a private ACR Task agent pool when isolated; existing registries leave private build connectivity to consumers.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Terraform registry defaults private and cannot form a public standard platform.
scenarioAssessments.blockedReason: Terraform registry public_network_access_enabled defaults false with a private endpoint in the mandatory VNet, preventing standalone-standard.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Registry exists, but no ACR Task agent pool or equivalent private-build handoff is present.

capabilities.title: Log Analytics, Application Insights, and AMPLS
capabilities.description: Create/reuse observability resources, secure existing connection string, mixed-workspace guard, private AMPLS, IDs, and runtime telemetry values.
identityRbacAssertions: Existing connection strings are secure inputs and are not emitted in inventory or outputs.
networkAssertions: Bicep optionally deploys AMPLS and monitor/opinsights/automation DNS zones only in isolated local-workspace deployments.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Terraform cannot deploy the public standard landing-zone topology.
scenarioAssessments.blockedReason: Terraform observability remains part of a mandatory private landing-zone topology, so it cannot represent standalone-standard.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: No Application Insights/AMPLS equivalent was found; Terraform exposes only the Container Apps Environment Log Analytics dependency.

capabilities.title: Managed identity and automatic RBAC
capabilities.description: Deployment principal type, system/user-assigned identity choice, per-workload API-key option, and automatic cross-service/control-plane/data-plane RBAC.
identityRbacAssertions: Bicep creates explicit deployment-user, service-identity, per-workload, cross-service, and Cosmos data-plane assignments.
API keys are Key Vault references and never stored as plaintext App Configuration values.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Identity support does not overcome Terraform's mandatory network topology.
scenarioAssessments.blockedReason: Terraform identity/RBAC constructs are deployed only in its VNet/private-endpoint topology and cannot produce standalone-standard.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Some role maps exist, but there is no automatic cross-service and per-workload RBAC equivalent.

capabilities.title: Foundry hosted-agent prerequisites and deployment handoff
capabilities.description: Prepare/deploy flags, immutable image digest contract, existing registry contract, role mode, project/registry/network/private-build outputs, and downstream deployment object.
identityRbacAssertions: Bicep prepares project and registry RBAC but does not create the downstream data-plane agent identity/version.
Operator Project Manager is independently gated with a compatible true default; disabling it preserves project managed identity registry pull.
networkAssertions: The handoff reports whether private build is required and supplies subnet/jumpbox/agent-pool values.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: No hosted-agent handoff exists and Terraform cannot form the public standard topology.
scenarioAssessments.blockedReason: Terraform has no hosted-agent prerequisite/handoff contract and its Foundry resources require the private topology, preventing standalone-standard.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: No equivalent hosted-agent immutable deployment handoff, project/registry RBAC preparation, or private-build output exists.

capabilities.title: Feature flags, software bootstrap, zone redundancy, and preflight
capabilities.description: Remaining software, zone-redundancy, and feature output contracts plus deployment-shaping preflight behavior.
networkAssertions: Bicep preflight validates mode/network/BYO combinations before deployment.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Terraform has no corresponding standard scenario to validate.
scenarioAssessments.blockedReason: Terraform's structural private topology means no preflight selection can produce Bicep standalone-standard.

scenarioAssessments.consumerImpact: Terraform validations differ and do not expose Bicep software/bootstrap or general zone-redundancy controls.
